However annoying "the game that inspired Balatro" might be for the developer, it's a good description. There's no metagame unlocks. There's just spinning the wheel, picking up new symbols and relics as you go. This means you have limited ability to steer your "build" and should be more concerned with engines and local synergies. It's still fun, and worth the few euros the dev charges for it. 
It also runs well on Steam Deck and Linux.

It is clear to see how this was the inspiration for Balatro. It isn't as fleshed out as Balatro and is based more around chance as you build your engine but it is enjoyable, quick and makes you want to come back for more. The retro graphics are charming and there are multiple paths to victory once you grasp how the many options play off of each other.
If it weren't for roguelikes based on gambling games, I'd have a horrible gambling problem. Small technical issues aside, this game is so much fun!

This is a fun little game if you can get it for cheap. I seem to remember that I got this when it first came out for something like 2 dollars. That's what my recommendation is based on. This game is fun at first, gives the satisfaction of getting new stuff (symbols and to a lesser extent items) and watching number go up. There's not a lot of replayability though. There's very few symbols that have the sort of scaling you need to make it through the late game, and symbol removal is so limited that you can't afford to take too many useless symbols. Lots of symbols have one specific item that makes them okay, but it's unlikely that you'll see that item. If you try to 100 percent this game, be prepared for a long grind where you click through menus looking for the same few symbols run after run after run. (At least there's a skip animations option but it's still a grind.) My recommendation is that you wishlist this game and pick it up if and when it goes on sale.

Overall very worth playing!

A great deckbuilder game, comparable to Crop Rotation which I also greatly enjoyed. Luck be a Landlord (LbaL) has a lot more RNG to it, which is appropriate considering the slot machine mechanism for determining placements of symbols. 5 columns with 4 rows totals 20 symbols displayed, and certain symbols have adjacency bonuses to other symbols to raise more money to pay your ever rising rent costs. External items can improve symbols gold production too, helping steer the player into more focused strategies. Rerolls help seek key pieces to finishing a strategy, and removals can get rid of low performing symbols to keep money production maximized. 
 
Sadly, once you defeat your landlord, all challenge is gone. I suppose there is some excitement in seeing how much money you can produce a turn, but it feels purely sandbox. Once you figure out a couple of good builds or strategies to go for even rank 20 starts to become a trivial challenge. 
 
If you're looking for a fun deckbuilder with more RNG than strategy I think Luck be a Landlord is a great fit. I have had a lot of fun even though it is a little more simple compared to other titles in the genre.

This game is essentially a slot machine roguelike. You start a run with a slot machine with mostly empty symbols, and then add a symbol every spin. There are dozens of synergy strategies to go for, and most games you will need to go for like 4 or 5 of them. There are no meta upgrades, but there are 20 difficulties you slowly unlock. Runs tend to be pretty fast, around 10 minutes. 
 
While the basic premise is pretty good, its the balance and replayability that really sells it. Early in a run you have to take symbols you might want to skip because else you'll fail the early money checks, but then when you have enough symbols you become more selective and try to synergies of your early mediocre picks. Its a really good system, where early decisions are making the best of a bad situation and midgame is all about course correcting. Then in the late game you can achieve those absurd, hyper efficient spins of the slot machine that feel really good and powerful. And while the game does have a luck element, even at the highest difficulty you can achieve about a 50% success rate. Since games also only take 10 minutes, and if you are going to fail can usually take under 5, failure also doesn't feel so bad. 
 
So the gameplay is good, addictive fun, but everything else is ok. The art is basic though does have some charm, but there is no real sound or music to speak off. And there is no real story either.  
 
For the low price this game is asking, the gameplay is worth it. Its a perfect

Good game. Binged the the heck out of it and got a hearty 17 hours out of it, which isn't too shabby. The presentation of the game is fairly simple. The menu/controls are nothing to write home about. The sprites are simple yet charming in their own way. All in all, an excellent example of good gameplay triumphing over graphics. Ran fine on the Steamdeck. Helped scratch that Balatro itch. 
 
The gist of the game is, each symbol/icon on the slot machine gives you at least one gold coin, most of the time, after a spin. Different icons/symbols interact with each other to give you more gold by incrementing or doubling values. It's your job to collect enough gold coins after X spins to pay your rent, which increases each time. You start out with a third of the slot machine filled out and after spinning you're given the opportunity to add one of a few random symbols to the slot machine. The strategy is choosing symbols that synergize with each other. You also get items (artifacts) that augments slots.  
 
RNG is obviously a factor so you can't guarantee a build will work out but if you take advantage of the preselected symbols and try planning for a couple different builds you can typically pivot into one of them if you think about the long game. Most symbols are viable, especially on the lower floors. Floors range from 1 to 20 with extra handicaps placed on you as you ascend.
